newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha easier, Europe cargoes add pressure.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha easier, Europe cargoes add pressure.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices were easier in Monday afternoon trade, trailing softer crude and naphtha prices in overseas markets on Friday, traders said.

Open-spec naphtha for second-half May was assessed at $230.00/232.00, down from Friday's levels of $232.50/234.50, while first-half June was at $228.00/230.00, compared with the previous level of $230.00/232.00.
Traders said an influx of cargoes from Europe was weighing on nearby contracts, in effect weakening inter-month spreads.
First-half May/first-half June was assessed at $3.50/4.50 after switching hands at $4.50 on Friday, traders said.
The one-month spread from second-half May was assessed at $3.00/4.00.

One trader said an estimated 200,000 tonnes of naphtha would be shipped from Europe to Asia in April and May respectively. "May seems to be oversupplied, but I personally doubt the spread will dip below $3.00," he said.

Traders said upcoming ethylene plant turnarounds in Japan and South Korea, and increased domestic naphtha production, were bearish for the market. However, traders said they were certain Asian naphtha demand would remain strong, as supply sources are limited. --Tokyo Energy Desk +81-3-5473-3708
